# PART A. Core product (v1)

## A1. Summary

TinyVigo is a web map of Vigo at Christmas. You open it from wherever you are, pick what you want to see, and it gives you a few walking routes that fit your time. Every Christmas point has a small pixel-art scene, a short story and its real schedule. Daily events can be added to the route. At the end you can turn a photo of yourself into a pixel-art postcard of Vigo.

It is built for people walking around the centre with a phone, so it has to work on mobile first and in the evening.

## A2. Approach

The product has two layers. A real satellite map gives orientation. Pixel-art scenes cover the places that matter, one per Christmas point.

There is no single painted map of the whole city. Repainting an aerial render with an image model gives a flat illustration with thin outlines and a washed palette, and it needs a fix at every tile seam. Close-up scenes work much better, and sprites made from the real photo of each decoration keep the real place recognisable.

Principles:
- **Current or labelled.** Every Christmas point shows where it is this year. If a location is not confirmed, the app says so.
- **Estimates and schedules are labelled as such.** Nothing that is a model or a timetable is presented as a live measurement.
- **Every number has an age.** Live data always shows when it was last updated.
- **No dependency on one feed.** If a feed fails, the map and the planner still work.

## A3. Look and feel

All scenes follow one reference look, described here in words.

The reference scene: an isometric view from about 45 degrees above, of a cobbled Galician square on a rainy winter night. In the middle stands a large Christmas tree covered in warm white lights with a golden star on top. Around it are four- and five-storey granite buildings with dark red tile roofs and dormer windows. White glass galleries (the typical Galician miradores) glow yellow from inside, and wrought-iron balconies and ground-floor arcades add detail. Garlands of small warm bulbs are strung between the buildings and the lamp posts. Wooden market stalls with red-lit goods and a small bandstand sit near the tree, with benches and ornate black street lamps that cast round halos. The wet cobblestones reflect all of it, with puddles. About twenty tiny people in coats and hats, some with umbrellas, are scattered over the square. Rain streaks are faintly visible, and a corner of dark navy sky shows at the top.

What makes it work:

- Warm night. Deep navy and brown shadows, golden light from windows, lamps and garlands, terracotta roofs, grey-brown granite, white galleries.
- Hard-edged chunky pixels, a limited palette and a little dithering on wet ground and roofs. People are tiny, a few percent of the frame height. Shapes are defined by colour and shade, with no thin dark outline around every object.
- Dense small life: people, stalls, benches, lamps, garlands.
- One main subject, large and central, taking roughly 40 percent of the frame height. The surroundings are plausible Vigo architecture, granite and glass galleries.
- Wide frame (16:9).

What to avoid: a high, zoomed-out aerial view where hundreds of buildings have the same size, thin black outlines on everything, flat pale ochre walls and terracotta roofs everywhere, and a daytime look. It reads as a flat illustration and not as pixel art.

One style for everything: scenes, sprites, icons, postcard and UI. No icons drawn in code next to painted art. This includes the icons of the data layers (car parks, weather): they are painted in the same style.

Text is never drawn by the image model. Labels, titles and postcard captions are set in code with a pixel font.

## A4. Features

### F1. Map

The base is the real satellite orthophoto (PNOA, 25 cm) with pan and zoom. On top go the Christmas points as pixel-art sprites, the lights as an animated layer, and the user's position if they allow it.

- Two base modes: Satellite and Night. Night is the same orthophoto darkened and tinted, with the lights switched on at their real hours.
- The lights come on at the schedule published by the Concello. Before the switch-on they stay off. (For 2026 the agenda JSON lists "Acto de encendido de luces de Navidad" at Porta do Sol on 2026-11-14, so the first lit night is today.)
- Layers that can be toggled: Christmas points, events, car parks. Christmas points and events are on by default.
- Car park layer: the 12 car parks from the Concello feed, each showing free spaces and a percentage, with the time of the last update. A car park that has not updated for a long time is shown as "no data", not with its last value.
- A small status strip shows the weather now and for the next hours (F6).
- Every Christmas point sits at its researched location (F2), checked by hand against the satellite image.

Acceptance: on a mid-range phone the map pans at a steady frame rate with the default layers on, and the first view loads in under 3 seconds on 4G (to be measured). No request from the browser goes to a plain-HTTP address or directly to a city feed.

### F2. Christmas points, their data and their story

**Source of truth.** The points are our own dataset, `points.json`, built by research (tickets R-01 to R-05). It is NOT a copy of the Concello's ArcGIS layer: that layer is the 2025-26 edition and is out of date. Changes this year already known from direct observation: the ferris wheel has changed location, the Cíes Market stalls have changed location, and new Disney items have arrived. There may be more, which is why every point is researched and not assumed.

The Concello layer (about 43 points: attractions, exhibits, light installations, photo galleries, Christmas markets, Santa and the Three Kings, photocalls) is used only as a starting checklist, if it can be found (ticket R-06). Its exact URL is not located yet. It may also contain 3D models of the attractions rather than only points; that is not confirmed. In either case TinyVigo does not use those 3D models: the app has its own pixel-art sprites and scenes, and only needs positions and schedules.

**Record for each point** (`points.json`):
- `id`, `name` (Galician, Spanish, English), `type` (attraction, exhibit, light installation, photo gallery, market, Santa or Three Kings, photocall, ride, show, other)
- `lat`, `lon`, `coord_method` (hand-placed on satellite, on-site GPS, source coordinates), `coord_accuracy_m`
- `schedule` (days, opening and closing times, show times, closed dates), `price` (free, paid, amount)
- `description_short`, `description_long`, `photo` (our own photo preferred), `sprite`, `scene`
- `story_card` (see below) with `sources`
- `status`: `confirmed_official` (the Concello publishes it for this year), `confirmed_multi` (at least three independent sources agree, or seen on site), `press_only` (one or two press sources), `unverified`, `removed` (existed before, not this year)
- `sources`: list of every source used, each with URL, publication date and what it said
- `last_verified` (date) and `verified_by` (research, on-site)

**Research protocol** (the work of tickets R-01 to R-05):
1. Build the candidate list: last year's points, the 2026-27 official programme (hoxe.vigo.org, the Concello's news service xornal.vigo.org, the tender documents for the Christmas decoration and attractions, which list the elements and their locations), Turismo de Vigo, the Concello's social profiles, local and regional press (several outlets), Google Maps and Street View, OpenStreetMap, listings sites, blogs and visitor guides.
2. For each point, compare many websites and record what each one says about the location and the schedule, with its publication date. Prefer sources dated 2026. Discard or flag anything that clearly describes an earlier edition.
3. Resolve conflicts in this order: the Concello's current official publication, then on-site observation (dated photo), then agreement of several independent recent sources, then single sources. Never average coordinates from sources that disagree on the place.
4. Place the coordinates by hand on the satellite image and, when possible, on the street, with the accuracy noted.
5. A point is shown on the map as confirmed only with status `confirmed_official` or `confirmed_multi`. A `press_only` point is shown with the label "not yet confirmed by the Concello". `unverified` and `removed` points are not shown.
6. Re-verify the dataset before launch and every week during the season, and after any Concello announcement. Schedules change (closures, weather, events).
7. Keep a research log (a file with every source and date) so any value can be traced and redone.

Acceptance: every point shown has a status above `unverified`, at least three sources recorded or an on-site check, and a verification date within the last 7 days of the season.

**Story cards.** Each point also has a short story card, three to five sentences, about where the tradition comes from or why it is there. The set of cards read in order tells the history of Christmas in Vigo.
- Every historical claim carries a source link. A card without a source is not shown. The cards are written by us from sources, not generated and published unchecked.

### F3. Preview a point

Tap a point on the map and a panel opens with:

1. The pixel-art scene of that place.
2. The real photo, one tap away, so the scene is never taken for a photograph.
3. Schedule for today and the next days, and whether it is on now.
4. The story card.
5. How to get there from the user's position (walking), and a button to add it to the route.
6. The nearest car park with its current occupancy and the time of the update, when the feed is available.
7. The confirmation status of the location and the date it was last verified.

The scene is generated once per point, offline, and stored as an image. It is not generated when the user taps. Scenes start with the landmarks (Porta do Sol tree, the Alameda, García Barbón street, the Vialia attractions) and grow from there. A scene for a point is made only after the location of that point is verified (ticket R-02), because the scene uses a satellite crop of its surroundings and the real photo.

How a scene is made: the real photo of the point plus a satellite crop of its surroundings go to the image model with a fixed style reference image (a scene that meets the look above) and a prompt that fixes light, palette and pixel size. Models tend to copy the layout of the style reference, so the prompt must say to keep the real surroundings of the point. A person reviews each result against the photo before it ships. Anything the model invented that changes the identity of the place (a tower that does not exist, a wrong roof) is rejected and redone.

### F4. Daily events

A list and a map layer of what is happening today, with a date picker for the next days.

- Sources: the Concello's cultural agenda and the time slots inside our points dataset (for example the tree's music-and-light shows and the Disney+ parade on García Barbón on 14 Nov at 17:00).
- The agenda is published as JSON, CSV and XLS (datos.gob.es and datos.vigo.org). The "today" file, `https://datos.vigo.org/data/axenda/agenda-hoy.json`, was verified on 2026-11-14 and contained 44 events. Its fields are: `id`, `titulo`, `fecha_inicio`, `fecha_fin`, `ciclo`, `permanente`, `subcategoria`, `direccion`, `imagen`, `instalacion`, `orden_pertenencia`. **It has no coordinates and no clock times.** The file name suggests it covers only today, so the date picker needs the multi-day agenda datasets (`agenda-cultura`, `agenda-turismo` in the CKAN catalogue) or a history that we build ourselves. Which dataset gives future days has to be confirmed (ticket D-03).
- Events get a location by joining the `instalacion` field to a venue dataset in the CKAN catalogue (for example `centros-culturales`, `turismo-poi` and the `distritos-*` datasets of theatres, auditoriums, museums, libraries, cinemas and parks). If the ID does not match, fall back to matching by venue name, then by the `direccion` text. If all fail, the event appears in the list but not on the map, and unmatched events are logged so the join can be improved (ticket D-04).
- Clock times for Christmas shows come from `points.json`, not from the agenda. If an agenda event has no time, show "time to be confirmed" and do not let it become a fixed-time stop.
- Permanent items (`permanente` set) and cycles (`ciclo`) are shown in their own group so long-running exhibitions do not flood the daily list.
- Filters: date, time of day, category, free entry, near me.
- Each event has a place, start and end time, and a button "Add to route". Added events become fixed-time stops.
- Examples confirmed on 2026-11-14: id 336 "Acto de encendido de luces de Navidad" (Porta do Sol) and id 4036 Disney+ parade on Avenida de García Barbón.

### F5. Route planner (walking)

Input: a starting point (the user's location or an address), a time window ("tonight from 19:00 to 22:30"), and the stops they picked (points and events). Walking only in v1.

Output: three route options, each with a total time, walking distance, ordered stops and a plain explanation of what it optimises.

1. Fastest: shortest total time visiting all chosen stops.
2. After dark: puts the light installations at the hours they are on, and the daytime-only points first. Streets near light installations are preferred, and long unlit stretches are avoided.
3. Easy walk: avoids the steepest streets (Vigo is hilly) and long stretches without a bench or a café.

How it works: it is a small ordering problem (up to about 12 stops), so an exact search is enough. Events are time windows that the route must respect. Walking times come from a pedestrian graph built from OpenStreetMap. If a chosen stop cannot be reached in time, the planner says which one and proposes dropping it instead of silently skipping it.

Signals that adjust the options (all optional inputs; if one is missing the planner still works and says which signal was missing):

- Slope: from the CNIG MDT05 elevation model, used by "Easy walk" (ticket D-11).
- Benches and cafés: from OpenStreetMap, used by "Easy walk".
- Light points and their hours: from `points.json`, used by "After dark".
- Weather: hourly rain probability and wind (F6). With rain in the window, the planner prefers shorter walks and covered streets (arcades, galleries) where OpenStreetMap marks them, and shows a rain warning on the route summary.
- Car park occupancy (F1): if the car parks near the centre are above 90 percent, the route summary suggests arriving by public transport. This is a hint, not a constraint, and v1 does not plan the public-transport leg (Part B).

Acceptance: for the same input the planner returns the same three routes (weather and parking hints may change the text of the summary, never the order, unless the user changed the input); with an event pinned at 20:00 no option arrives after 20:00; it answers in under 2 seconds for 12 stops.

### F6. Weather and status strip

- Source: Open-Meteo (no key needed). If it fails, the strip shows the last good value with its age, then hides itself.
- What is shown: now, the next 6 hours, and rain probability for the route window.

### F7. Postcard

The user uploads or takes a photo, picks a place from the Christmas points, and optionally writes a short message and a name. They get a pixel-art postcard of that place with themselves in it.

Pipeline:
1. A vision model describes the photo as structured data: how many people, rough clothing and colours, pose, mood. No identification of anyone.
2. An image model receives the person photo, the scene of the chosen point and the style reference, and draws the person in the scene in the same pixel style.
3. The frame, the "Greetings from Vigo" title, the name and the message are added in code, never by the model.
4. The user downloads a PNG and can share it. The postcard has a small credit line and the date.

Rules: the uploaded photo and the result are not kept on the server after the request ends, unless the user chooses to save. A short notice tells people their photo goes to a third-party model. Each device gets a daily limit and the service has a monthly spending cap, because every postcard costs money.

## A5. Data sources for v1

| Data | Source | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Satellite imagery | PNOA orthophoto, IGN, CC BY 4.0 | Available |
| Streets, shops, benches, cafés | OpenStreetMap, ODbL | Available |
| Elevation | CNIG MDT05 (WMS, WMTS, WCS) | Documented |
| Christmas points and schedules | Our researched `points.json` (tickets R-01 to R-05) | To be built |
| Christmas layer baseline (optional) | Concello ArcGIS Hub, edition 2025-26 | Out of date; URL not located (R-06) |
| Cultural agenda | `https://datos.vigo.org/data/axenda/agenda-hoy.json` and agenda datasets in CKAN | Verified for today; future days to confirm |
| Venues for the agenda join | CKAN: `centros-culturales`, `turismo-poi`, `distritos-*` | Documented |
| Car park occupancy | `https://datos.vigo.org/data/trafico/parkings-ocupacion.json` | Verified (12 car parks) |
| Weather | Open-Meteo | Available |

The Concello's official 2026-27 Christmas programme was approved recently, so points and dates change. The research tickets and the weekly re-verification keep the data current, and the app shows the date the data was last verified.

## A6. Verified feed details used in v1

- **Car parks** (`parkings-ocupacion.json`): array of 12 objects with `id`, `id_parking`, `nombre`, `lat`, `lon`, `plazaslibres`, `totalplazas`, `ocupacion` (percent) and `fechahora` (format "2026-11-14 11:39:01"). Sample: Parking Náutico Cíes, 114 free of 180, 37 percent. The real refresh rate is not measured (the CKAN metadata says "daily" for feeds whose names suggest 3 to 5 minutes).
- **Agenda, today** (`agenda-hoy.json`): 44 events with the fields listed in F4.
- The Concello catalogue (CKAN, 172 datasets, licence ODC-BY) is at `https://datos-ckan.vigo.org`, with files served from `datos.vigo.org/data/...`.

## A7. Architecture and how feeds are consumed

Components:
- A static front end (map, scenes, UI) served from a CDN or the existing VPS.
- A small server for the parts that cannot be static: route planning and postcard generation. It holds the model credentials, so none of them reach the browser.
- The **snapshot publisher**: a small scheduled job on the same server that fetches the city feeds and publishes them as static files.
- Scenes, sprites and icons are generated offline and checked into the repo as images with the prompt and source photo next to them, so anyone can redo one.

**Decision on feeds: snapshot publisher.** A scheduled job (a cron job or a systemd timer on the VPS) does the following for each feed:
1. Fetch the feed at its own interval.
2. Validate the payload (expected fields, sane ranges, not empty). Reject a bad payload and keep the previous good one.
3. Write a static JSON snapshot with `fetched_at`, the source's own timestamp when it has one, and the data.
4. Append a row to a history file (used later by the busy estimate in Part B).
5. If a fetch fails, keep serving the last good snapshot. The app compares `fetched_at` with the current time and shows the age; after a threshold it shows "no data".

The app reads only these static files from our own domain.

Intervals in v1:

| Feed | Interval | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Car park occupancy | 5 minutes at most, never faster than its measured real refresh | Set after D-00 |
| Weather (Open-Meteo) | 30 minutes | |
| Agenda | Every night and once at midday | |
| Points dataset | Rebuilt when the research log changes | Not a feed |

Why this option and not the others:
- Browser calls the city feed directly: rejected. The Concello endpoints may not allow cross-origin requests, plain-HTTP sources cannot be called from an HTTPS page, and every visitor would hit the Concello's server.
- A proxy that fetches on every user request: rejected. It adds latency, multiplies requests to the Concello on busy evenings, and gives no history.
- A live connection (websocket or streaming): rejected. The feeds are polled files, so there is nothing to stream, and the extra complexity does not pay off.
- Snapshot publisher: chosen. It is simple, nearly free, protects the Concello's servers, survives feed outages, keeps API keys server-side, makes freshness explicit and builds a history at no extra cost.

Notes:
- The traffic totals file (Part B) has no timestamp in its payload, so for any such feed the age is our fetch time only and the UI must not present it as more precise than that.
- All data reuse follows the licences: the Concello data is ODC-BY, so every screen or the About page credits it.

Decision needed before the postcard goes live: how the server authenticates and pays for the image model. A long-lived server credential has to be set up (an API key with prepaid balance, or a Vertex AI service account), and the key must never reach the browser. Nothing else in the spec depends on this.

## A8. Non-functional

- Mobile first, readable outdoors at night, one-handed.
- Languages: Galician, Spanish, English. Strings are not hard-coded.
- Text in the UI is real text, with enough contrast against the dark map. Pixel art never carries information that is not also in text. Occupancy and weather are always also given as words or numbers.
- Credits for OpenStreetMap, IGN and the Concello (ODC-BY), and for any other source used, on an About screen (ticket D-17).
- Freshness is visible: every data layer shows when it was last updated, and every point shows when its location and schedule were last verified (ticket D-18).
- Estimates are labelled as such; the unconfirmed state of a point is shown.
- No account, no tracking beyond privacy-friendly page counts.
- Performance: first view under 3 seconds on 4G (to be measured); planner under 2 seconds for 12 stops; a failing feed never slows the first view.

## A9. Out of scope for v1

- Repainting the whole city or every building as pixel art.
- Anything about buses and trains (timetables, arrivals, routes, transit legs): see Part B.
- Real GPS positions of Vitrasa buses (not published).
- Measured crowd, footfall or queue data (no open source exists).
- Ticket sales, bookings, user accounts.
- Anything outside Vigo and its Christmas season.

## A10. Build order (v1)

Time estimates, not measured.

0. Research and data checks (starts immediately and runs in parallel with everything else): R-01 to R-05 (the attractions research) and D-00 (measure the feeds). The scenes depend on the verified locations of the first landmarks, so R-02 comes first.
1. Data and base map (about 1 day): load `points.json` (even with partial data), satellite, map with points, schedules and the "on now" state; car park layer; freshness UI.
2. Scenes for 6 landmarks (about half a day, plus review), after R-02 has verified their locations: prove the look described above before making the rest. If these six do not look right, rethink the approach before building anything else.
3. Preview panel and story cards (about 1 day, plus the time to research the stories).
4. Events (about 1 day): agenda loader and venue join.
5. Route planner (about 1 day, plus half a day for the signals).
6. Postcard (about 1 day, after the payment decision).
7. Remaining scenes, in batches, as time allows.

## A11. Open questions

- View angle. This spec reads "satellite view" as a top-down real map with pixel-art scenes opening from it. If the idea was an isometric map of the centre instead, F1 changes, and keeping tiles consistent across seams becomes a requirement.
- Who is it for first: tourists, or people from Vigo? It changes the story cards and the default language.
- Name and domain. `tinyvigo` is a working name.
- Season end date. The Concello's closing date for the lights decides how long the project stays useful.
- Photos of the attractions: take our own on site (best, no copyright problem and they feed F3 and the scenes) or use others' photos with permission?

---

# PART B. Extras (v1.1 and v2)

None of these blocks v1. They are ordered by how useful they are. Tickets are in Part C.

## B1. Public transport (v2)

The two integrations moved out of v1: **buses** (Vitrasa: times, arrivals, routes) and **trains** (Renfe: arrivals and times). When they come in, they also bring transit legs in the route planner ("walking plus bus"), the next departures at the nearest stop or station in the point panel, and the bus-stop and train-station layers on the map.

- **Vitrasa (buses).** GTFS from the Concello (CKAN `gtfs-vitrasa`, with `paradas-vitrasa` and `lineas-vitrasa`), ODC-BY. This is the theoretical timetable, not GPS positions, and the UI must say "scheduled", not "live". Moovit attributes its Vitrasa data to the Concello under that same licence. There is no official open real-time Vitrasa feed. The only live sources found are unofficial wrappers of the company's SOAP service (VigoBusAPI, Time for Vbus API); they carry legal and terms-of-use risk and can break, so if ever used they are optional, cached, labelled unofficial and nothing depends on them.
- **Renfe (trains).** Static GTFS for Alta Velocidad, Larga y Media Distancia (`https://ssl.renfe.com/gtransit/Fichero_AV_LD/google_transit.zip`, CC BY 4.0, 700 KB, includes Vigo-Urzáiz and Vigo-Guixar) and a separate Cercanías GTFS (commuter trains, for example Vigo to Redondela). Check that the Vigo stops are present.
- **Renfe live.** The Cercanías real-time alerts feed is published at `https://gtfsrt.renfe.com/alerts.pb`, with companion trip-update and vehicle-position feeds. They respond, but coverage of Vigo is unverified, and the feeds are protobuf, which the research tools could not decode. The long and medium-distance feed URLs are not confirmed. Verify before showing anything live; until then trains are scheduled only. Renfe also runs a public real-time map at `tiempo-real.renfe.com` (a website, not an API).
- Intercity and metropolitan buses run by the Xunta (the intermodal bus station at Vialia): no open GTFS found. CKAN has `t-navieras` (ferries) and `t-tren` (rail information from the Concello).
- Because the Christmas mobility plan cancels some bus stops in the centre (Colón, García Barbón, Areal, Policarpo Sanz, Alameda and Cánovas del Castillo are listed as cancelled stops in the Concello's plan), the stop data must be cross-checked with that plan before showing a stop as usable during Christmas.

## B2. Buildings layer (v1.1)

The Concello's 3D buildings, to show footprints and heights at street zoom and to add data to the story cards.

- Located and read (verified): ArcGIS Feature Service `https://services9.arcgis.com/ss3qikvq575kYKRJ/arcgis/rest/services/Edificios_3D_de_Vigo_en_vectorial/FeatureServer`, layer 0 "EDIFICIOS" (item id `1196c4f7cdfa478eb9ac09b1fffc2576`), and a Scene Service at `.../SceneServer` (item id `fe74b88f9dec4669aab30a3f3aef1274`).
- Geometry is 3D (MultiPatch) in ETRS89 UTM 29N (WKID 25829), so coordinates must be reprojected to WGS84; at most 2000 records per request, so the loader pages through it.
- Fields: `refcat` (cadastral reference), `distrito`, `seccion`, `barrio`, `parroquia`, `ano_antiguedade` (year built), `ano_reforma`, `uso_principal_superficie`, `cc_residencial`, `cc_industrial`, `cc_oficinas`, `cc_comercial`, `superficie_total`, `superficie_residencial`, `superficie_industrial`, `superficie_oficinas`, `superficie_comercial`, `altura` (height), `z`, `interes_turismo`, `habitantes`, `riesgo_inund_1m`, `riesgo_inund_2m`, `riesgo_inund_3m`, `is_fxcc`, `radiacion_anual`.
- Not confirmed: whether the service returns GeoJSON for MultiPatch, its licence, and how complete `altura` is. A one-time offline conversion produces a footprint-plus-height file; the fallback is the Catastro INSPIRE footprints joined by `refcat`.
- Extra uses: `interes_turismo` to flag landmark buildings for scenes and cards, `ano_antiguedade` for stories about old buildings, `uso_principal_superficie` and `superficie_comercial` to mark shopping streets.
- These services were found through the Concello's portal search API (see C1), which also lists the hotels service `https://datos.vigo.org/arcgis/turismo/poi-hoteles-gl/FeatureServer/0`.

## B3. Busy-now estimate (v2)

A coarse estimate of how busy each main zone is (Porta do Sol, Gran Vía and Vialia, Alameda, the old town). It is NOT a count of people: no open real-time footfall source exists for Vigo, and the Concello's own visitor figures come from mobile-phone data that is not published as open data. It is an estimate built from open proxies and the interface says "estimate".

- Inputs: car park occupancy (the strongest signal), traffic state, today's agenda and show times, weekday or weekend or holiday, weather, and Celta home matches at Balaídos (29 Nov 2026 Villarreal, 3 Jan 2027 Deportivo, 21 Mar 2027 Real Madrid, 21 Apr 2027 Barcelona; from press, to be confirmed against the league calendar).
- Output: three levels per zone (quiet, normal, busy) and a hint of the usual quiet hours.
- Calibration: the snapshot publisher's history (A7) is the data to tune it. MITMA mobility data (C2) seeds typical patterns once.
- Acceptance: the word "estimate" is always visible; no number of people is ever shown; with two or more inputs missing, it hides itself.
- It does not contradict "measured crowd data" being out of scope: it is a labelled model.

## B4. Traffic layer and cameras (v1.1)

- **Traffic state:** `https://datos.vigo.org/data/trafico/treal_totales.json` (verified: 5 states from "Muy lento" to "Muy fluido" with metres of road per state; no timestamp in the payload) and `https://datos.vigo.org/data/trafico/treal.geojson` (unverified, returned binary data). Shown as coloured road segments if the segment file is usable, otherwise as a single city-wide indicator in the status strip.
- **Cameras:** `https://datos.vigo.org/data/trafico/camaras-trafico.json` (verified: 61 cameras with `id`, `nombre`, `url`, `lat`, `lon`). The image URLs are plain HTTP (`http://camaras.vigo.org/webcam/camv2.php?id=05`), so they cannot be embedded in an HTTPS page. Either fetch the image through our server (only if the Concello's terms allow it) or show an outbound link.

## B5. Alerts (v1.1)

- Road incidents on the main access roads from the DGT National Access Point, DATEX II v3.7 (`https://nap.dgt.es/datex2/v3/dgt/SituationPublication/datex2_v37.xml`), CC-BY, refresh every five minutes, state road network only (AP-9, A-55, A-52 accesses), not urban streets. The older v3 dataset is deprecated, so use v3.7.
- City notices from the Concello (CKAN `t-avisos`, `t-avisos-transporte`) that mention closures during events or parades.
- Both in one alerts list and, with a position, on the map.

## B6. Weather backups and tides (v1.1)

- AEMET OpenData: free API key; two calls per request (the first returns a URL for the data); municipal forecast for Vigo uses code 36057.
- MeteoGalicia MeteoSIX v5: hourly numerical forecast (key required), station current state, hourly history, and a tides JSON where Vigo is port id 3.
- Failover: if Open-Meteo fails, switch to a backup and show which one is in use. Tides only matter for coastal walks.

## B7. Traffic tiles from TomTom (v2, optional)

Flow and incident tiles. The free plan gives 50,000 tile and 2,500 non-tile requests per day, no card, commercial use allowed; over the limit the API returns 429. Needs attribution and the snapshot approach or a caching proxy so a busy evening does not use the allowance.

## B8. Historical mobility (v2)

MITMA mobile-phone big-data study: open CSVs with origin-destination matrices by district, hourly, in continuous publication since 2020. District granularity, not real time. Use: typical December flows into the centre, to seed B3. INE publishes similar mobility studies.

## B9. Other ideas (not planned, kept for later)

- Concello notices and mobility plan as content: the plan for the centre during Christmas (cancelled bus stops, peripheral car parks) is a document, not a feed, but is useful to read into the route hints.
- Other ArcGIS services of the Concello (tourism points, markets, bike lanes, schools) found through the portal search API (ticket X-12).
- Waze: no official open feed for Vigo was found; third-party "Waze APIs" are scrapers and are excluded.
- Foreseeable season extensions: Reyes Magos (Three Kings) and the last days of the lights.

# PART C. Data catalogue and ticket backlog

## C1. Concello de Vigo data

Portal: `https://datos.vigo.org`. Catalogue: `https://datos-ckan.vigo.org` (CKAN, 172 datasets, licence ODC-BY). Maps: `https://mapas.vigo.org` (built on ArcGIS Hub). 3D digital twin: `https://mapas.vigo.org/pages/gemelo-digital-3d-vigo`. Developers: `https://datos.vigo.org/reutilizadores/`. Request channel for new data: on datos.vigo.org ("Envía a túa aplicación").

What "ArcGIS" means here: the Concello stores its geographic datasets as ArcGIS "feature services", which are web endpoints that return points, lines or polygons with their attributes as JSON, readable with a plain HTTP request. The portal's search API lists them:

`https://mapas.vigo.org/api/search/v1/collections/all/items?q=<words>&limit=<n>` returns GeoJSON with each item's id, type and service URL; item details are at `.../items/<id>`. Verified, no key needed. Use it one request at a time: several parallel requests were rate limited. A search for `edificios` found the buildings and hotels services; a search for `navidad` returned nothing; other words (`nadal`, `luces`, `atracciones`) were blocked by rate limiting and still have to be tried.

CKAN datasets relevant to the project (names as listed; contents not opened unless said):
- Transport: `gtfs-vitrasa`, `lineas-vitrasa`, `paradas-vitrasa`, `t-aparcabicis`, `t-carrilesbici`, `t-carga-descarga`, `t-estado-trafico`, `t-camaras`, `t-parking`, `t-parking-real`, `t-taxis`, `t-tren`, `t-navieras`, `t-avisos`, `t-avisos-transporte`, `t-gasol`, `parking-discapacitados`, `puntos-recarga`.
- Culture, tourism and agenda: `agenda-cultura`, `agenda-turismo`, `centros-culturales`, `turismo-poi`, `turismo-aloj`, `turismo-com`, `turismo-res`, `comercio-mercados`, `playas`, and the `distritos-*` datasets.
- Base data: `callejero-vigo`, `avisos`, `urbanismo-cartografia` (DXF; the link is flagged as broken).
- Other themes available: `seguridad-*`, `salud-*`, `educacion-*`, `deportes-*`, `ma-*`, `lp-*`, `poblacion-2019-*`, `e-paro-*`.

Christmas information: the official page is `https://hoxe.vigo.org/navidad/nadal_vigo.php` (it did not open as readable text with the research tools), the Concello's Instagram profile is `navidadvigooficial`, and the Concello publishes a downloadable lights map each year. The Concello's mobility plan for the centre during Christmas is on `xornal.vigo.org`.

## C2. Other sources

- Open-Meteo (weather, no key). AEMET OpenData and MeteoGalicia (see B6). DGT NAP (B5). TomTom (B7). MITMA and INE (B8). Renfe Data (B1). AENA publishes monthly Vigo-Peinador statistics (context only).
- PNOA orthophoto and CNIG MDT05 (WMS, WMTS, WCS), Catastro INSPIRE (WFS, ATOM), OpenStreetMap, Cartociudad (geocoding, not checked). Xunta open data portal `abertos.xunta.gal` (tourism offices, restaurants, georss feeds; not checked in detail).
- Not found: an open real-time Vitrasa feed, an open Xunta bus GTFS, any open crowd or footfall data, the Concello's Christmas layer URL.

## C5. Risks

- The Concello publishes the 2026-27 programme in pieces and some changes only appear in the press, so locations and schedules can still change after launch. Mitigation: R-05, the visible verification date and the status label.
- Conflicting sources about where an attraction is. Mitigation: the conflict rules in F2 and on-site checks.
- The Concello metadata says "daily" for feeds that look like 3 to 5 minute feeds. Real freshness is unknown until D-00.
- The agenda has no coordinates or times. A weak venue join would leave many events off the map.
- Rate limiting of the Concello's sites (seen on mapas.vigo.org during the research): the snapshot publisher must fetch politely, one request at a time, with back-off.
- The Concello's Christmas layer may never be located. It is only a baseline, so this does not block v1.
- Unofficial Vitrasa real-time wrappers can break or be blocked: Part B only, never a dependency.
- The busy estimate can be wrong and visitor figures are politically sensitive: Part B only, labelled as an estimate.
- Free tiers (TomTom, AEMET keys) can run out on a busy evening: Part B only, cached.

    def add(
        self,
        *,
        id: str = "",
        title: str = "",
        description: str = "",
        criteria: str = "",
        depends_on: str = "",
    ) -> AgentResult:
        """Añade una feature al backlog. `criteria` y `depends_on` van separados por `;`."""
        missing = []
        if not id:
            missing.append("¿Qué id le pongo? (ej. API-002)")
        if not title:
            missing.append("¿Cuál es el título de la feature?")
        if not criteria:
            missing.append("¿Cuáles son los criterios de aceptación? Sepáralos con ';'.")
        if missing:
            return self._fail("add", "Faltan datos para añadir la feature.", needs=missing)

        if self._geas_enabled():
            return self._add_geas(id, title, description, criteria, depends_on)

        doc, error = self._load()
        if doc is None:
            return self._fail("add", error)
        if self._find(doc, id) is not None:
            return self._fail("add", f"Ya existe una feature con id '{id}'.")

        feature = {
            "id": id,
            "title": title,
            "description": description or title,
            "acceptance_criteria": [c.strip() for c in criteria.split(";") if c.strip()],
            "status": "pending",
            "depends_on": [d.strip() for d in depends_on.split(";") if d.strip()],
        }
        unknown = [d for d in feature["depends_on"] if self._find(doc, d) is None]
        if unknown:
            return self._fail(
                "add", f"depends_on apunta a features que no existen: {', '.join(unknown)}."
            )

        doc["features"].append(feature)
        self._save(doc)
        return AgentResult(
            success=True,
            agent=self.name,
            action="add",
            message=f"{id} añadida al backlog ({len(feature['acceptance_criteria'])} criterios).",
            data=feature,
        )

    def _add_geas(
        self, identifier: str, title: str, description: str, criteria: str, depends_on: str
    ) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            if geas_backlog.find(self.ctx.root, identifier) is not None:
                return self._fail("add", f"Ya existe una feature con id '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
        except geas_backlog.GeasUnavailable as exc:
            return self._fail("add", f"GEAS no disponible: {exc}")

        criteria_list = [c.strip() for c in criteria.split(";") if c.strip()]
        deps = [d.strip() for d in depends_on.split(";") if d.strip()]
        for dep in deps:
            try:
                if geas_backlog.find(self.ctx.root, dep) is None:
                    return self._fail(
                        "add", f"depends_on apunta a features que no existen en GEAS: {dep}."
                    )
            except geas_backlog.GeasUnavailable as exc:
                return self._fail("add", f"GEAS no disponible: {exc}")

        try:
            created = geas_backlog.create_feature(
                self.ctx.root,
                feature_id=identifier,
                title=title,
                description=description or title,
                criteria=criteria_list,
                depends_on=deps,
            )
        except geas_backlog.GeasUnavailable as exc:
            return self._fail("add", f"No se pudo crear el ticket: {exc}")

        warnings = self._refresh_mirror()
        return AgentResult(
            success=True,
            agent=self.name,
            action="add",
            message=(
                f"{identifier} añadida a GEAS ({str(created.get('id', ''))[:8]}) "
                f"con {len(criteria_list)} criterios."
            ),
            data={**created, "id": identifier},
            warnings=warnings,
        )

def find(root: Path, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Busca por id de feature (``SCOPE-001``) o por UUID de ticket."""
    items = tickets(root)
    by_ticket = {str(t.get("id") or ""): t for t in items}
    if _uuid(identifier):
        ticket = by_ticket.get(identifier)
        return to_feature(ticket, by_ticket) if ticket else None
    for ticket in items:
        if feature_id(ticket) == identifier:
            return to_feature(ticket, by_ticket)
    return None


def is_blockable(ticket: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    return str(ticket.get("status") or "").upper() in BLOCKABLE


def repository_id(root: Path) -> str:
    """Repo de este checkout, resuelto por ``.geas.yml`` o por el único visible."""
    cfg = _config(root)["cfg"]
    declared = str(cfg.get("repository_id") or "")
    if declared:
        return declared
    repo = str(cfg.get("repository") or "")
    if repo and not (root / ".geas.yml").is_file():
        (root / ".geas.yml").write_text(f"repository: {repo}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    try:
        return load(root).resolve_repository(root)
    except GeasError as exc:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"resolve_repository: {exc}") from exc


def build_description(description: str, criteria: list[str]) -> str:
    parts = [(description or "").strip()]
    if criteria:
        parts.append(
            CRITERIA_HEADER + "\n" + "\n".join(f"  {i}. {c}" for i, c in enumerate(criteria, 1))
        )
    return "\n\n".join(p for p in parts if p)


def create_feature(
    root: Path,
    *,
    feature_id: str,
    title: str,
    description: str,
    criteria: list[str],
    depends_on: list[str],
    priority: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Crea un ticket en GEAS. Las dependencias deben existir ya (UUID)."""
    client = load(root)
    repo = repository_id(root)
    deps: list[str] = []
    for dep in depends_on:
        found = find(root, dep)
        if not found or not found.get("ticket_id"):
            raise GeasUnavailable(f"La dependencia '{dep}' no existe en GEAS.")
        deps.append(str(found["ticket_id"]))
    try:
        created = client.create_ticket(
            title=f"{feature_id}: {title}",
            description=build_description(description, criteria),
            repository_id=repo,
            dependencies=deps,
            priority=priority,
        )
    except GeasError as exc:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"create_ticket: {exc}") from exc
    return {**created, "feature_id": feature_id}


def start(root: Path, identifier: str, commit_before: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
    found = find(root, identifier)
    if not found:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"No existe la feature '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
    try:
        result = load(root).start_ticket(str(found["ticket_id"]), commit_before)
    except GeasError as exc:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"start_ticket: {exc}") from exc
    return {**found, **result}


def complete(
    root: Path, identifier: str, commit_after: str = "", result_text: str = "OK"
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    found = find(root, identifier)
    if not found:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"No existe la feature '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
    try:
        result = load(root).complete_ticket(
            str(found["ticket_id"]), commit_after=commit_after, result=result_text
        )

def write_mirror(root: Path, features_list: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None) -> bool:
    """Escribe el espejo solo si cambió. Devuelve True si lo reescribió."""
    features_list = features(root) if features_list is None else features_list
    target = root / "harness" / "featureslist.json"
    new = document(root, features_list)
    text = json.dumps(new, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
    try:
        current = target.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        current = ""
    if current == text:
        return False
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    return True


def find(root: Path, identifier: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Busca por id de feature (``SCOPE-001``) o por UUID de ticket."""
    items = tickets(root)
    by_ticket = {str(t.get("id") or ""): t for t in items}

# MeshHarmes

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12+-blue?logo=python&logoColor=white)
![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-0.1.2-green)
![Author](https://img.shields.io/badge/Author-cacelass-blueviolet)

> Arnés de agentes e infraestructura de proyecto para trabajo general en Python.

Un repositorio para empezar proyectos donde el trabajo lo hace —en parte— un
agente de IA, con las reglas del juego escritas **en código** y no en un
prompt: una puerta de entrada que decide si se puede trabajar, un backlog con
criterios de aceptación, memoria fuera de la ventana de contexto y una puerta
de permisos para las acciones que no se deshacen.

No incluye nada de un dominio concreto. El paquete `app/` está vacío a
propósito: ahí va tu código.

# CI de MeshHarmes — ejecuta lo mismo que `make check`, más el arnés.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  quality:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.12", "3.13"]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync --extra dev --frozen

      - name: Lint
        run: |
          uv run ruff check app/ tests/ agents/
          uv run ruff format --check app/ tests/

      # Sin `--strict` en la línea: la configuración vive en pyproject.toml.
      # Pasarlo aquí haría que CI y tu máquina comprobasen cosas distintas.
      - name: Type check
        run: uv run mypy app/ tests/

      - name: Test
        run: uv run pytest tests/ -v --cov=app --cov-report=xml

      # Bloqueante a propósito: el arnés exige evidencia para cerrar una
      # feature, pero sus propios tests podían romperse sin que CI se enterase.
      - name: Agent tests
        run: uv run pytest agents/tests/ -v --tb=short

      # La puerta del arnés, en CI. Sin --quick no aportaría nada: los tests
      # ya se ejecutaron arriba y el fallo saldría dos veces.
      - name: Harness gate
        run: |
          chmod +x init.sh
          ./init.sh --quick

      # Los prompts de los agentes se derivan del código y de contracts.py.
      # Si alguien añade una acción y no regenera, esto lo caza.
      - name: Prompts in sync
        run: uv run python -m agents.prompts_sync

      # Solo las suites deterministas: `smoke` ejecuta la acción principal de
      # cada agente y depende del estado del repo, así que no mide nada estable.
      - name: Agent evals
        run: uv run python -m agents.evals.runner --harness --routing --contracts

      - name: Security scan
        run: uv run bandit -r app/ -f txt -x tests
        continue-on-error: true

      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v5
        with:
          file: ./coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

    def _finish_geas(
        self, identifier: str, evidence: str, changes: str, decisions: str, pending: str
    ) -> AgentResult:
        try:
            feat = geas_backlog.find(self.ctx.root, identifier)
        except geas_backlog.GeasUnavailable as exc:
            return self._fail("finish", f"GEAS no disponible: {exc}")
        if feat is None:
            return self._fail("finish", f"No existe la feature '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
        if str(feat.get("raw_status") or "") == "DONE":
            return self._fail("finish", f"'{identifier}' ya está en done en GEAS.")

        gate = self.gate()
        if not gate.success:
            return self._fail(
                "finish",
                f"NO se cierra '{identifier}': la puerta no pasa. {gate.message}",
                data=gate.data,
                warnings=gate.warnings,
            )
        if not evidence:
            return self._fail(
                "finish",
                f"'{identifier}' no se cierra sin evidencia.",
                needs=[
                    "Pega la salida real del comando que demuestra cada criterio "
                    "(pytest, make check, ./init.sh). Una afirmación no es evidencia."
                ],
            )

        head = git_sync.current_head(self.ctx.root)
        warnings: list[str] = []
        dirty = git_sync.is_dirty(self.ctx.root)
        if dirty:
            warnings.append(
                "El árbol tiene cambios sin commitear: GEAS guarda el HEAD actual "
                "como commit_after. El commit de cierre va después con "
                "`git commit_feature`."
            )

        try:
            geas_backlog.complete(
                self.ctx.root,
                identifier,
                commit_after=head,
                result_text=(evidence.strip().splitlines()[0][:200] if evidence.strip() else "OK"),
            )
        except geas_backlog.GeasUnavailable as exc:
            return self._fail("finish", f"GEAS no cerró '{identifier}': {exc}")

        gate_line = gate.data.get("checks", []) if isinstance(gate.data, dict) else []
        pytest_line = next(
            (c["detail"] for c in gate_line if c.get("check") == "pytest"), "init.sh en verde"
        )
        closed = date.today().isoformat()
        entry = (
            f"\n## {identifier} — {feat.get('title', '')}\n\n"
            f"- **Cerrada:** {closed}\n"
            f"- **Verificación:** ./init.sh en verde · {pytest_line}\n"
            f"- **Ticket GEAS:** {str(feat.get('ticket_id', ''))[:8]} · commit_after `{head[:8]}`\n"
            f"- **Cambios:** {changes or '_(no indicados)_'}\n"
            f"- **Decisiones:** {decisions or '_(ninguna reseñable)_'}\n"
            f"- **Pendiente:** {pending or '_(nada)_'}\n\n"
            f"<details><summary>Evidencia</summary>\n\n```\n{evidence.strip()}\n```\n\n</details>\n"
        )
        self._progress_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with self._history_file.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(entry)
        self._current_file.write_text(IDLE_CURRENT, encoding="utf-8")
        warnings.extend(self._refresh_mirror())

        return AgentResult(
            success=True,
            agent=self.name,
            action="finish",
            message=(
                f"{identifier} cerrada en GEAS ({str(feat.get('ticket_id', ''))[:8]}). "
                "Histórico actualizado y current.md en idle."
            ),
            data={
                "id": identifier,
                "closed": closed,
                "ticket_id": feat.get("ticket_id"),
                "commit_after": head,
            },
            warnings=warnings,
        )

    def finish(
        self,
        *,
        id: str = "",

        decisions: str = "",
        pending: str = "",
    ) -> AgentResult:
        """
        Cierra una feature. REHÚSA si ./init.sh no pasa en verde: es la regla
        del arnés, y aquí es código, no una instrucción que se pueda ignorar.
        """
        if not id:
            return self._fail(
                "finish",
                "Falta el id de la feature.",
                needs=["¿Qué feature cierro? Usa su id de featureslist.json."],
            )

        if self._geas_enabled():
            return self._finish_geas(id, evidence, changes, decisions, pending)

        doc, error = self._load()
        if doc is None:
            return self._fail("finish", error)

        feat = self._find(doc, id)

def complete(
    root: Path, identifier: str, commit_after: str = "", result_text: str = "OK"
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    found = find(root, identifier)
    if not found:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"No existe la feature '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
    try:
        result = load(root).complete_ticket(
            str(found["ticket_id"]), commit_after=commit_after, result=result_text
        )
    except GeasError as exc:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"complete_ticket: {exc}") from exc
    return {**found, **result}


def block(root: Path, identifier: str, reason: str = "") -> dict[str, Any]:
    found = find(root, identifier)
    if not found:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"No existe la feature '{identifier}' en GEAS.")
    try:
        result = load(root).block_ticket(str(found["ticket_id"]), reason)
    except GeasError as exc:
        raise GeasUnavailable(f"block_ticket: {exc}") from exc
    return {**found, **result}

        """Invoca una herramienta MCP por HTTP. Levanta GeasError si falla."""
        url = f"{self.base_url}/api/tools/{tool}"
        body = json.dumps(params or {}).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST")
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if self.token:
            # El proxy lo convierte en X-Geas-Actor.
            req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {self.token}")
        if self.actor_id:
            # Acceso directo (esta máquina, sin proxy).
            req.add_header("X-Geas-Actor", self.actor_id)
        if self.org_id:
            req.add_header("X-Geas-Organization", self.org_id)
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=self.timeout) as resp:
                raw = resp.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            raw = exc.read()
            try:
                payload = json.loads(raw or b"{}")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                raise GeasError(f"HTTP {exc.code}: {raw[:200]!r}") from exc
        except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
            raise GeasError(

    def start_ticket(self, ticket_id: str, commit_before: str = "") -> dict:
        t = self.storage.get_ticket(ticket_id)
        if not t:
            return _err(f"Ticket no encontrado: {ticket_id}")
        denied = self._authorize(t.organization_id, "ticket:start")
        if denied:
            return denied
        denied = self._authorize(t.organization_id, "resource:lock")
        if denied:
            return denied
        if t.status != TicketStatus.FREE:
            return _err(f"Ticket no está FREE: {t.status.value}")
        if not self.storage.are_dependencies_resolved(ticket_id):
            return _err("DEPENDENCIES_UNRESOLVED")

        acquired, blocked_resource = self.storage.acquire_locks(
            t.resources, ticket_id, self.actor_id
        )
        if not acquired:
            lock = self.storage.get_lock_for_resource(blocked_resource or "")
            return _err(
                "RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE",
                {
                    "resource_id": blocked_resource,
                    "locked_by": lock.ticket_id if lock else "",
                },
            )

        branch = f"{ticket_id[:8]}-{self._safe_branch(t.title)}"
        self.storage.start_ticket(
            ticket_id,
            commit_before=commit_before,
            branch=branch,
            actor_id=self.actor_id,
        )
        self.storage.create_event(
            Event(
                event_type="TICKET_STARTED",
                organization_id=t.organization_id,
                actor_id=self.actor_id,
                resource_type="ticket",
                resource_id=ticket_id,
                metadata={"branch": branch, "commit_before": commit_before},
            )
        )
        return _ok({"id": ticket_id, "status": "IN_PROGRESS", "branch": branch})

    def block_ticket(self, ticket_id: str, reason: str = "") -> dict:
        t = self.storage.get_ticket(ticket_id)
        if not t:
            return _err(f"Ticket no encontrado: {ticket_id}")
        denied = self._authorize(t.organization_id, "ticket:block")
        if denied:
            return denied
        self.storage.update_ticket_status(ticket_id, "BLOCKED")
        self.storage.create_event(
            Event(
                event_type="TICKET_BLOCKED",
                organization_id=t.organization_id,
                actor_id=self.actor_id,
                resource_type="ticket",
                resource_id=ticket_id,
                metadata={"reason": reason},
            )
        )
        return _ok({"id": ticket_id, "status": "BLOCKED"})

    def complete_ticket(
        self, ticket_id: str, commit_after: str = "", result: str = ""
    ) -> dict:
        t = self.storage.get_ticket(ticket_id)
        if not t:
            return _err(f"Ticket no encontrado: {ticket_id}")
        denied = self._authorize(t.organization_id, "ticket:complete")
        if denied:
            return denied
        denied = self._authorize(t.organization_id, "resource:unlock")
        if denied:
            return denied
        # GEAS-005: mismo motivo que en create_ticket: el cambio de estado, la
        # liberacion de locks y el evento van juntos o no va ninguno.
        with self.storage.transaction():
            self.storage.complete_ticket(
                ticket_id, commit_after=commit_after, result=result
            )
            released = self.storage.release_locks_for_ticket(ticket_id)
            self.storage.create_event(
                Event(
                    event_type="TICKET_COMPLETED",
                    organization_id=t.organization_id,
                    actor_id=self.actor_id,
                    resource_type="ticket",
                    resource_id=ticket_id,
                    metadata={"commit_after": commit_after, "locks_released": released},
                )
            )

finish called `geas_backlog.complete(...)` which called `client.complete_ticket(...)` which calls the server's complete_ticket tool. """Permite `python -m app`."""

import sys

from app.cli import main

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
=== cli ===
"""
app.cli — punto de entrada del proyecto: `python -m app` o `make run`.

Un esqueleto, no un framework: argparse de la stdlib y un subcomando de
ejemplo. Si tu proyecto no es una CLI, borra este fichero y `__main__.py` —
el arnés no los necesita.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from collections.abc import Sequence

from app import __version__


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="app", description="Proyecto MeshHarmes.")
    parser.add_argument("--version", action="version", version=f"%(prog)s {__version__}")

    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    hello = sub.add_parser("hello", help="Comando de ejemplo: saluda y sale.")
    hello.add_argument("--name", default="mundo", help="A quién saludar.")

    return parser


def hello(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hola, {name}."


def main(argv: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.command == "hello":
        print(hello(args.name))
        return 0
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Importar el paquete app no ejecuta la CLI ni mata el proceso (FIX-001)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pkgutil

import app
import app.__main__  # noqa: F401 — regresión: importar no debe ejecutar la CLI


def test_walk_packages_sobre_app_no_mata_el_proceso() -> None:
    modulos = [m.name for m in pkgutil.walk_packages(app.__path__, prefix="app.")]
    assert "app.__main__" in modulos
    assert "app.cli" in modulos
"""La CLI de ejemplo arranca, saluda y devuelve 0."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from app.cli import build_parser, hello, main


def test_hello_devuelve_el_saludo() -> None:
    assert hello("MeshHarmes") == "Hola, MeshHarmes."


def test_main_imprime_y_sale_con_cero(capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]) -> None:
    assert main(["hello", "--name", "arnés"]) == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "Hola, arnés."


def test_sin_subcomando_es_error_de_uso() -> None:
    # argparse sale con código 2 en errores de uso: no lo tratamos como éxito.
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        build_parser().parse_args([])
    assert exc.value.code == 2

        paths.TESTS_DIR,
        paths.DOCS_DIR,
        paths.HARNESS_DIR,
        paths.VAULT_DIR,
    ):
        assert path.parent == paths.ROOT_DIR

    assert paths.ensure_dir(destino) == destino
    assert paths.ensure_dir(destino) == destino
    assert destino.is_dir()

"""
app.paths — rutas del proyecto, resueltas una sola vez.

Existe por un motivo concreto: en cuanto dos módulos calculan por su cuenta
"dónde está la raíz", uno de los dos se equivoca el día que cambia la
estructura. Aquí la raíz se deriva de la posición de este fichero, así que
funciona igual desde un test, desde un script y desde `python -m app`.

`agents/context.py` hace el mismo cálculo para el arnés y a propósito no
importa este módulo: los agentes tienen que poder trabajar aunque el paquete
del proyecto no importe.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

#: app/paths.py -> parents[1] es la raíz del repositorio.
ROOT_DIR: Path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

PACKAGE_DIR: Path = ROOT_DIR / "app"
TESTS_DIR: Path = ROOT_DIR / "tests"
DOCS_DIR: Path = ROOT_DIR / "docs"
HARNESS_DIR: Path = ROOT_DIR / "harness"
VAULT_DIR: Path = ROOT_DIR / "vault"


def ensure_dir(path: Path) -> Path:
    """Crea el directorio si no existe y lo devuelve. Idempotente."""
    path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return path

{
  "content": "# Arquitectura — TinyVigo\n\n> Rellenado por `DESIGN-001`. Fuente: spec TinyVigo v3 (Part A7, Part B).\n\n## Piezas del sistema\n\n1. **Frontend estático** (mapa, escenas, UI): servido desde CDN o el VPS existente. Mapa satélite PNOA, puntos como sprites pixel-art, capa de luces animada, posición del usuario.\n2. **Servidor pequeño** (Python): planificación de rutas y generación de postales. Guarda las credenciales de los modelos; nada llega al navegador.\n3. **Snapshot publisher**: job programado (cron/systemd timer) en el mismo servidor que descarga los feeds de la ciudad, los valida y publica snapshots JSON estáticos que la app lee.\n4. **Escenas offline**: generadas una vez por punto, guardadas como imágenes en el repo junto al prompt y la foto fuente.\n5. **Dataset `points.json`**: fuente de verdad de los puntos navideños, construido por investigación (R-01..R-05).\n\n## Flujo\n\n```\nUsuario (móvil) → Frontend estático (CDN)\n   ├── lee snapshots JSON (nuestro dominio) ← Snapshot publisher ← feeds ciudad\n   ├── mapa satélite (PNOA) + sprites\n   └── para rutas/postal → Servidor Python → modelos de imagen (credenciales server-side)\n```\n\nEl navegador nunca llama a un feed de la ciudad ni a un modelo. Todo pasa por nuestro dominio o por el servidor.\n\n## Alternativas consideradas y descartadas\n\n- **El navegador llama al feed de la ciudad directamente**: rechazado. Los endpoints del Concello pueden no permitir CORS, las fuentes HTTP no se pueden llamar desde HTTPS, y cada visitante golpearía el servidor del Concello.\n- **Proxy que descarga en cada petición del usuario**: rechazado. Añade latencia, multiplica peticiones al Concello en noches de mucho tráfico y no genera historial.\n- **Conexión en vivo (websocket/streaming)**: rechazado. Los feeds son ficheros polled; no hay nada que streamear y la complejidad no compensa.\n- **Repintar toda la ciudad como pixel art**: rechazado. Un render aéreo repintado da una ilustración plana con contornos finos y paleta lavada, y necesita un apaño en cada costura de tile. Las escenas cercanas funcionan mucho mejor.\n\n## Riesgos conocidos\n\n- El Concello publica el programa 2026-27 a trozos y algunos cambios solo aparecen en prensa: ubicaciones y horarios pueden cambiar tras el lanzamiento (mitigación: R-05, fecha de verificación visible, etiqueta de estado).\n- Fuentes contradictorias sobre dónde está una atracción (mitigación: reglas de conflicto en F2 y comprobación in situ).\n- Los metadatos del Concello dicen \"diario\" para feeds que parecen de 3–5 minutos; la frescura real se desconoce hasta D-00.\n- El join de sedes para la agenda puede dejar muchos eventos fuera del mapa si es débil.\n- Rate limiting de los sitios del Concello (observado en mapas.vigo.org): el publisher descarga con cortesía, una petición a la vez, con back-off.\n- El layer de Navidad del Concello puede no localizarse nunca: es solo una línea base, no bloquea v1.\n- Los wrappers no oficiales de Vitrasa pueden romperse o bloquearse: solo Part B, nunca dependencia.\n- La estimación de afluencia puede ser errónea y las cifras de visitantes son sensibles: solo Part B, etiquetada como estimación.\n- Los tiers gratuitos (TomTom, claves AEMET) pueden agotarse en una noche de mucho tráfico: solo Part B, cacheado.\n\n## Decisiones diferidas (Part B y posteriores)\n\n- Transporte público (autobuses Vitrasa, trenes Renfe): v2. Incluye patas de tránsito en el planner, próximas salidas y capas de paradas/estaciones.\n- Huella de edificios y alturas (capa 3D del Concello): v1.1.\n- Estimación de afluencia (\"busy-now\"): v2, siempre etiquetada como estimación.\n- Backups de tiempo (AEMET, MeteoGalicia) y mareas: v1.1.\n- Tiles de tráfico TomTom: v2, opcional.\n- Movilidad histórica MITMA: v2.\n- Tráfico y cámaras: v1.1.\n- Alertas (DGT DATEX II, avisos del Concello): v1.1.\n- Autenticación y pago del modelo de imagen para postales: decisión pendiente antes de publicar postales.\n- Ángulo de vista (mapa satélite vs isométrico): pregunta abierta A11.\n- Público objetivo primario (turistas vs vigueses): pregunta abierta A11.\n- Nombre y dominio (`tinyvigo` es nombre de trabajo): pregunta abierta A11.\n- Fecha de fin de temporada (cierre de luces): pregunta abierta A11.\n- Fotos de las atracciones (propias vs con permiso): pregunta abierta A11.\n\n## Stack\n\n- Lenguaje: Python 3.12+ (el .venv de referencia es 3.13)\n- Entorno y dependencias: uv (uv.lock)\n- Calidad: ruff, mypy, pytest, bandit, pip-audit\n- Conocimiento: vault Obsidian + graphify + RAG local opcional (chromadb)\n- Frontend: estático, mapa satélite PNOA, escenas pixel-art generadas offline\n- Servidor: Python (rutas + postales), credenciales server-side\n- Datos: snapshots JSON publicados por job programado\n\n## Estructura del repositorio\n\n```\ntinyvigo/              — Código del proyecto (TinyVigo)\ntests/                 — Tests del proyecto\nagents/                — Sistema multi-agente del arnés (stdlib pura)\nharness/               — El arnés: backlog, progreso, memoria\nvault/                 — Conocimiento estable (Obsidian)\ndocs/                  — Sphinx\n```\nEOF\necho written",
  "path": "/home/cancelas/NaviHack/vault/01_PROYECTO/arquitectura.md"
}

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _cache_dir(self) -> None:
        CacheTool.set_cache_dir(GraphifyTool.cache_dir(self.ctx.root))

    def _gather_project_text(self) -> str:
        """Junta el texto del que se extraen las keywords: README + pyproject + grafo."""
        parts: list[str] = []
        for path in (self.ctx.readme_file, self.ctx.pyproject_file):
            if path.exists():
                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                    parts.append(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
        # Etiquetas de los nodos más centrales del grafo, si graphify ya corrió.
        if GraphifyTool.graph_exists(self.ctx.root):
            try:
                graph = GraphifyTool.load_graph(self.ctx.root)
                adj = GraphifyTool._adjacency(graph)
                nodes = GraphifyTool._node_index(graph)
                top = sorted(adj, key=lambda n: len(adj[n]), reverse=True)[:20]
                parts.extend(str(nodes.get(nid, {}).get("label", "")) for nid in top)
            except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — grafo ausente/corrupto no debe romper esto
                pass
        return "\n".join(parts)

    def project_keywords(self, *, top: int = 12) -> AgentResult:
        """Extrae las palabras clave que describen el proyecto."""
        text = self._gather_project_text()
        if not text.strip():
            return AgentResult(
                False, self.name, "project_keywords",
                "No encontré README ni pyproject.toml de los que extraer keywords.",
            )
        keywords = ResearchTool.extract_keywords(text, top=top)
        return AgentResult(
            True, self.name, "project_keywords",
            f"{len(keywords)} palabra(s) clave del proyecto: {', '.join(keywords)}",
            data={"keywords": keywords},
        )

    def search(self, *, query: str, backend: str = "openalex", max_results: int = 10,
               no_cache: bool = False) -> AgentResult:
        """Busca papers para una consulta concreta en un backend (arxiv|openalex)."""
        if backend not in _BACKENDS:
            return AgentResult(
                False, self.name, "search",
                f"Backend '{backend}' desconocido. Disponibles: {sorted(_BACKENDS)}.",
            )
        self._cache_dir()
        search_fn = _BACKENDS[backend]

        def _run() -> list:
            return search_fn(query, max_results=max_results)

        try:
            if no_cache:
                papers = _run()
            else:
                papers = CacheTool.disk_cache(name=f"research_{backend}_{query}_{max_results}")(_run)()
        except ToolExecutionError as exc:
            return AgentResult(False, self.name, "search", f"Búsqueda en {backend} falló (¿sin red?): {exc}")

        keywords = ResearchTool.extract_keywords(query, top=8) or query.split()
        ranked = ResearchTool.rank(ResearchTool.dedupe(papers), keywords)
        return AgentResult(
            True, self.name, "search",
            f"{len(ranked)} paper(s) en {backend} para '{query}'.",
            data={"backend": backend, "query": query, "papers": ranked},
        )

52:    def extract_keywords(text: str, *, top: int = 12, min_len: int = 4) -> list[str]:
    def extract_keywords(text: str, *, top: int = 12, min_len: int = 4) -> list[str]:
        """
        Palabras clave candidatas de un texto, por frecuencia. Determinista:
        tokeniza, descarta stopwords y palabras cortas, ordena por frecuencia
        (desempate alfabético para estabilidad).
        """
        words = re.findall(r"[a-zA-Záéíóúñü]+", text.lower())
        freq: dict[str, int] = {}
        for w in words:
            if len(w) < min_len or w in _STOPWORDS:
                continue
            freq[w] = freq.get(w, 0) + 1
        ordered = sorted(freq.items(), key=lambda kv: (-kv[1], kv[0]))
        return [w for w, _ in ordered[:top]]

    # -- búsqueda: arXiv ------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def search_arxiv(query: str, *, max_results: int = 10, timeout: int = 15) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Busca en arXiv y devuelve papers normalizados. Lanza si la red falla."""
        params = urllib.parse.urlencode({
            "search_query": f"all:{query}",
            "start": 0,
            "max_results": max_results,
            "sortBy": "relevance",
            "sortOrder": "descending",
        })
